citation.sourceDocument: IRS Publication 15 (2026), Employer's Tax Guide, §7; IRC §3402(g); Treas. Reg. §31.3402(g)-1
citation.sourceNote: Pub. 15 (2026): "The withholding rate on supplemental wages remains 22% (37% if supplemental wages paid to an employee during the calendar year exceed $1 million) because P.L. 119-21 permanently extended the individual tax rates". §7: supplemental wages over $1 million in a calendar year are "subject to withholding at 37%", "without regard to the employee's Form W-4"; below that, an employer paying them separately from regular wages may withhold the optional flat 22%, or add them to regular wages and withhold on the total. Severance, bonuses and accrued vacation paid at separation are supplemental wages. The flat rate is a withholding rate, not the tax on the payment. Read 2026-10-19.
